additional_info.subject: Update
additional_info.body:
Dear Team: The Maximum charging current for outlets are limited to 250A via the charger configuration. Please refer PLC configuration.
Note: As long as the boost mode is not selected for the Outlets, the connector will only deliver 250A as maximum.
Do not change Boost setting. It’s pre-set in the factory and depends on the ordered hardware configuration. A change could overload the powertrain and results in a failure of the charger.

additional_info.subject: RE: AW: 0378125 - ID0378125-DC/Si-D/DE- [MP / PN 170001090]Low charging power at DC1 CRM:02023000136
additional_info.body:
Dear Team,
I hope you are doing well.
From the PLC configuration, we have learned that the maximum charging current for the outlets is limited to 250A.
Additionally, the boost mode has not been selected for the outlets, so the connectors will only deliver a maximum of 250A as per the current configuration.
We recommend not changing the boost setting, as it is pre-set at the factory based on the ordered hardware configuration. Altering this setting could potentially overload the powertrain and lead to charger failure.
Based on our analysis, we observed that the EV’s target current is 250A, and this demand has been fully met by the EVSE (charger).
Kindly refer to the attached snapshot, where you can see that the EVSE is providing exactly what the EV requested.
Regards,
Abhinav Malokar
eMobility Support
